To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PCGLS method is an efficient parallel algorithm for sparse least squares problems.
PCGLS and its IMGS preconditioner can be implemented in a highly parallel fashion on massively parallel distributed computers.
the PCGLS and the IMGS preconditioner are efficient methods to solve sparse least squares problems in a parallel environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of parallel methods for sparse least squares problems and their implementation on a parallel computer with distributed memory.
the parallelization of a basic iterative method for solving sparse least square problems on massively distributed parallel computers.
the parallelization of the iterative solution of large sparse systems of linear equations on parallel architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PCGLS method can be successfully implemented on massively parallel distributed-memory computers, but the performance is not satisfactory because of the global communications required for the inner-products.
the parallelization of the PCGLS and the IMGS preconditioner is effective and the parallel efficiency of these methods is good.
PCGLS and PC-IMGS are very efficient for sparse least squares problems with large number of unknowns and large condition number of the matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PCGLS is the best parallel method for solving sparse least-squares problems on massively parallel computers.
the parallelization of these methods is not difficult but the performance of the parallel implementation is limited by the communication time.
PCGLS is very efficient for solving large scale least squares problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to obtain the optimal performance of PCGLS method, the number of processors must be chosen in such a way that the number of inner products that are performed in the same time interval is equal to the number of processors, i.e., the number of processors is equal to the size of the system.
, with a proper parallelization of the preconditioner, the performance of the iterative method is comparable to that of the direct method on massively parallel distributed computers.
, in the case of sparse least squares problems, PCGLS with IMGS preconditioner is a very efficient method for parallel computing.
